label: YS-24
title: YS-22 fix DoS: tempPauser zero-gate in PostMigrationCleanup always reverts on any valid production run following a clean Step 1 broadcast
description: PostMigrationCleanup.s.sol line 351 now requires `tempPauserRecorded && recordedTempPauser != address(0)` as the story-065 YS-22 hardening. However, DeployTempStableStakerAndMigrators.s.sol line 256 reads `tempPauser = IStakerOwnable(address(tempStaker)).pauser()` BEFORE line 270-274 call `setPauser(OWNER_ADDRESS)` on the freshly deployed tempStaker. A freshly deployed StableStaker has `pauser == address(0)` at construction time (the constructor does not initialize the pauser role). The Deploy script captures address(0) and writes it to the JSON at line 303, as explicitly documented in lines 292-294 of the same file: 'A freshly deployed tempStaker pauser is address(0) by default; persist it anyway (cleanup treats a zero recorded temp pauser as restore to zero).' The story-065 zero-rejection gate in cleanup now CONTRADICTS this documented contract: on every clean Step 1 broadcast the JSON will contain `"tempPauser":"0x0000...0000"`, and cleanup will hard-revert at line 351 with 'YS-22: tempPauser not recorded (or zero)'. The entire migrate:ys-swap-cleanup entry point is permanently DoS'd without manual JSON surgery on any run that follows a clean Step 1 broadcast.
impact: migrate:ys-swap-cleanup is permanently unrunnable after a clean Step 1 broadcast. The migration cannot reach the final cleanup state: tempStaker phUSD mint authority is never revoked (PostMigrationCleanup.s.sol line 321), the original staker and tempStaker remain paused (blocking user deposits/withdrawals indefinitely), and pauser restoration for both stakers never executes. This is a DoS of the cleanup entry point that leaves the migration in a permanently halted state.
recommendation: Two valid fixes: (1) Remove only the `!= address(0)` condition from the tempPauser check — keep `tempPauserRecorded` but allow zero (since address(0) is the valid as-deployed tempStaker pauser, not an unrecorded error). The origPauser check is correct as-is since origPauser cannot legitimately be zero (guarded by require at Deploy line 262). (2) Alternatively, have Step 1 (DeployTempStableStakerAndMigrators) read tempPauser AFTER calling setPauser(OWNER_ADDRESS) on the freshly deployed tempStaker (move lines 256/258 after line 272), so it records OWNER_ADDRESS rather than address(0).
